newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: No takers for Philippine Yankee in secondary mart.
newsitem.headline: No takers for Philippine Yankee in secondary mart.

text.p: The newly launched Philippine yankee bonds had hardly been touched in Asian secondary trading with investors giving wide bid-and-offer quotes, bond traders said on Monday.
Sole underwriter Salomon Brothers was able to sell the bulk of the bonds to U.S. fund managers.
"We have bid-and-offer quotes as wide as 100 basis points," a senior trader at a large commercial bank told Reuters. Indicative bids were at 99, while offers were at 100 points.
The $400-million worth of 30-year Philippine Yankee bonds were issued at 99.908 on Thursday evening in London.
The $100 million, 100-year Yankee bond was not even quoted in the market. It was offered at 99.459.
The 30-year bond which was offered at 184.9 basis points above the prevailing 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was too tight for many investors, traders said.
"The Yankee bond is very illiquid. Nobody is willing to buy or sell at this level," the trader added.
The reaction conrasts with the fairly active trading for the 20-year Philippine Eurobond. Bids were at 101.75 while offers at 101.95.
A trader at a foreign bank said there was nothing inherently wrong with the Yankee bonds but foreign fund managers were not too keen on Asian debts while U.S. Treasuries were firming.
"They are revaluating things following a strong uptrend in the U.S. Treasuries," he said.
Another said she prefered peso-denominated government securities which have been very volatile following fresh Thai baht troubles late last week.

Bankers Trust, in its recent study, said Philippine bonds should be attractive for investors as they offer room for more spread tightening, which would traslate to higher pricing, due to the recent credit upgrade by Moody's Investors Services.
